summary: Okta SSO attribute mapping change caused RBAC role assertion to be blank; console login blocked for Infra engineers
description:
Issue summary:
Several Infra engineers were unable to access Redwood Console (authorization error) after an HR profile sync landed on 2026-03-01. Okta authentication completed but the app received an empty 'roles' SAML attribute, causing RBAC to deny access.

Impact:
- ~12 engineers in the Infra and Platform teams reported 'You are not authorized to view this page' even though they could authenticate via Okta.
- Blocking access to production observability dashboards and deployment tooling for a subset of on-call engineers during a 2.5 hour window.

Environment:
- Redwood Console (web UI) using SAML/OIDC with roles asserted via SAML attribute 'roles'.
- Affected region: prod us-west.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Sign in to console with an affected user account that normally maps to Infra role via Okta groups
2) Complete Okta SSO flow
3) Observe successful authentication but console shows authorization error (403 / "not authorized")

Observed behavior:
- SAML response from Okta did not include a 'roles' attribute for affected users (attribute present for other users).
- Okta System Log entries show successful SSO but the Group-to-Role mapping rule returned an empty array.

Expected behavior:
- SAML response includes roles claim (e.g., 'infra_eng', 'platform_admin') so RBAC can evaluate and grant access.

Initial workaround applied:
- Support manually granted console roles to 12 affected users via internal admin UI to restore access.
investigation_notes:
Timeline and findings:
- 2026-03-01 09:12 UTC: First support ticket opened by Aisha. Slack thread #internal-auth: https://slack.redwood.com/archives/C12ABC345 (see thread TS: 1612).
- 2026-03-01 09:25 UTC: Confirmed users could authenticate at Okta but roles claim missing in SAML assertion. Sample SAML (redacted) attached to internal ticket.
- 2026-03-01 09:40 UTC: Noted recent HR->Okta profile sync (daily job) ran at 08:58 UTC and included a schema change: department field converted to multi-valued array; Okta attribute mapping logic was brittle and matched on string equality.
- 2026-03-01 10:00 UTC: Reproduced locally by altering test Okta profile to use department as list; group rule returned no groups.
- Hypothesis: HR sync changed the underlying attribute shape (string -> array). The Okta group-to-role mapping condition relied on exact string match on 'profile.department' and skipped assignment when type changed.
- Evidence: Okta System Log event IDs: 0A1B2C3D4E (SAML assertion missing roles).
- Impact scope: 12 confirmed users, likely all users whose role assignment path used department-based mapping rather than group claim.
- Related GitHub PR addressing the brittle mapping and adding schema tolerant mapping: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-config/pull/422
- Linked internal ticket for follow-up automation to detect attribute shape changes: INT-9850.

2026-03-01 09:30 - Miguel Torres (oncall-auth): Investigating. Confirmed SAML response lacks roles claim for affected users. Escalating to identity team. Opening this ticket.

2026-03-01 10:05 - Priya Raman (identity-engineer): Found HR sync changed 'department' to multi-value array. Current mapping rule expects string equality. Proposing fix to mapping rule and adding tolerant matching.

2026-03-03 15:42 - Priya Raman: Merged fix to auth-config to treat department as array and to prefer explicit Groups claim for role assignment. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-config/pull/422. Planning rollout to prod config on 2026-03-04 02:00 UTC.
2026-03-05 08:10 - Miguel Torres: Verified rollout completed and no new access incidents reported. Closing incident and creating follow-up ticket INT-9850 for automated detection + runbook updates.
resolution:
Root cause: HR profile sync changed the 'department' attribute shape in Okta from a single string to a multi-valued attribute. Existing Okta attribute-to-role mapping was implemented with strict string equality and failed to map roles when attribute type changed.

Fix applied:
- Deployed updated Okta mapping logic that: (1) checks Groups claim first, (2) normalizes 'department' into a list and performs containment checks rather than string equality.
- Deployed auth-config change: https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-config/pull/422.
- Manually restored access for affected users while fix was prepared.

Rollout notes:
- Prod rollout executed 2026-03-04 02:00 UTC during low-traffic window. No rollback required.
- Post-deploy verification: sampled 30 users across infra/platform, all received roles correctly in SAML assertion.

Follow-ups / Action items:
- INT-9850: Add automated alert when Okta SAML assertions have missing expected attributes (schema drift detection).
- Update runbook: Confluence page updated with troubleshooting steps and search terms for Okta Syslog events.
- Add unit/integration tests to auth-config to simulate attribute shape changes.

Status: Resolved and monitoring.
postmortem_action_items: INT-9850 - implement SAML attribute schema drift alerting
Update runbook page with exact Okta Syslog event IDs and remediation steps
Add integration tests to auth-config for multi-valued attributes
Review HR->Okta sync change control process to require notification for schema changes
